analysis:
This batch contains only documentation: the new changelog.d/cluster-service-follows-repair.md (head 1-6) and a new section in docs/architecture/inference.md (head 3541-3575). No Swift source is in this batch, so the described behavior could not be verified here. Missing source limits coverage; it is not evidence that the change is safe.

Described behavior: ClusterService.listenerChange re-checks each setup and control-lease listener at most every 5 s (listenerCheckSeconds). It restarts a listener on a cable port/address change or a new pairing and stops it when no pairing remains. An unreadable pairing store leaves listeners unchanged (fail-static). Pairing.Identity compares both pins, the cluster label, the link epoch and the edge, but not the edge secret. ensureControl drops earlier control state when either the local or the peer member changes.

No regression is identified. The base behavior already kept the earlier pairing until the service restarted. Following the new pairing, and stopping when none remains, narrows how long a stale credential stays usable.

Questions for integration/source review in ClusterService.swift, ClusterServiceControl.swift and ClusterSetupLinkExchange.swift:
(1) Confirm that excluding the edge secret from Identity cannot let a re-pair with a changed secret but reused epoch keep the old key. The docs rely on every ceremony deriving a fresh epoch.
(2) Fail-static on an unreadable store keeps the old pairing's listener answering. If an operator unpairs and the store then becomes unreadable, the stale peer stays accepted until restart. This is likely acceptable but undocumented in the threat model.
(3) Confirm that a restart tears down in-flight sessions and leases authenticated under the old pairing.
(4) The control-lease listener restarts without a log line, which reduces auditability.

These cluster pairing and keyed-link listeners are not covered by any current TB or threat entry (closest are TB-003 and TB-007). The threat model may need a cluster-pairing boundary entry.
